//: Which files have been through the string sweep, and what may stay English. The swept list is a ratchet: a file joins it when its strings are converted, and from then on any new hardcoded UI text in it fails i18n:check. Converting 405 strings in one commit and turning the rule on at the end would mean a wall of failures nobody can act on; this way the gate tightens one file at a time and can never loosen.
//scan: Exactly the surfaces the sweep covers (I18N.md §1.1). An include list rather than exclusions, because the things left out are left out for a reason and a new file should have to argue its way in: apps/server/client/player.ts is frozen diagnostics on the /play page, the data and media adapters are developer-facing, and the routes' error strings become codes under §5.1 rather than catalogue entries.
//html: Files that are not .tsx but do contain markup, so the `>text<` pass should still run on them. `pages.ts` renders the server pages as HTML template literals. The pass is off by default for .ts because `a > b && c < d` is arithmetic and the span between the operators reads as element text — an opt-in list is safer than a heuristic that guesses which angle brackets are markup.
//namespaces: Key prefix per file, where the default (basename minus a Panel/Editor/Dialog suffix) reads badly. Keeping this explicit means a file rename does not silently re-key an entire panel's catalogue entries.
//allow: Text that is deliberately not translated even inside a swept file — product names, units, and the font sample in the layers panel. Kept short on purpose: every entry is a hole in the rule.

direction.//: I18N.md §6.1: surfaces pinned dir="ltr" keep physical properties on purpose. `files` is whole-file (a frozen page, or one that is nothing but graphic geometry); `selectors` are CSS selector prefixes inside a pinned subtree. Anything else uses a `dir-ok` line marker with a reason.
